extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, organizations, and individuals submitting comments on EPA dockets and rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for drafting and submitting public comments to EPA dockets (rulemakings and related documents), including procedural requirements, content-quality expectations, and restrictions. Focuses on using Regulations.gov, structuring arguments, supporting claims with evidence, and compliance with submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary Submission Method (Regulations.gov preferred)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations.gov is the EPA's preferred method of receiving comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although Regulations.gov is preferred, alternative formats are accepted through various mailing addresses. Use Regulations.gov when possible to ensure efficient receipt and processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification & Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the docket ID number and identifying information in your subject line to ensure your comment reaches the right location and isn't lost or misdirected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put the docket ID and clear identifiers in the subject line so staff can route your comment correctly; unclear or missing identifiers may cause misdirection or loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding & Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the document thoroughly before commenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are confused about the document, contact the EPA representative listed in the document and describe your difficulty in your response. Do background research so your comment addresses the actual proposal and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to any specific directions provided by the Agency, including responding to particular questions or organizing comments in requested formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Agency asks for responses to specific questions or a particular organization/format, follow those directions to make your input usable and aligned with the docket's needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Over Volume
rubrics_metrics.description: The comment process is not a vote – one well-supported comment is often more informative to the agency than a thousand form letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on substantive arguments rather than expressing simple agreement or disagreement. Well-reasoned, evidence-backed comments are prioritized over high volumes of identical form comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support Your Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain your position clearly using specific examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid profanity or personal threats. Where appropriate, suggest alternative language or solutions. Provide concrete examples to make your point persuasive and actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Base arguments on sound reasoning, scientific evidence, or documented personal impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When citing costs or burdens, explain your calculations in reproducible detail. Cite sources, data, or documented experiences to substantiate claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address Counterarguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge and respond to opposing viewpoints and trade-offs relevant to your position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss likely counterarguments and explain why your position should prevail given the trade-offs; this strengthens credibility and usefulness to the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet Deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments by the deadline specified in the Federal Register document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late submissions may not be considered. Verify the deadline in the Federal Register notice and plan to submit before that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited Content: Threatening Language or Profanity
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments with threatening language or profanity are rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid abusive, threatening, or profane content; such submissions will be removed and not considered in the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia Submissions Require Written Comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia submissions require accompanying written comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you submit audio, video, or other multimedia, include a written statement or transcript so the agency can readily digest and make the content part of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyrighted Material Requires Proof of Redistribution Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyrighted material needs proof of redistribution rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit copyrighted works unless you can show you have the right to redistribute them; otherwise the agency may reject or remove the material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Business Information (CBI) Handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential Business Information should not be submitted electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need to submit CBI, contact the EPA Docket Center at 202-566-1744 for guidance on appropriate submission methods and protections; do not include CBI in electronic docket submissions.
